Visit note | 2025-07-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Emon Ahmed, 25, male. Mr. Ahmed attends for review regarding his ongoing headaches where bright light hurts his eyes and he feels the need to lie in a dark room. He mentions his symptoms have been worse since starting night shifts at a hospital in Rajshahi. He works as a nurse and notes his sleep schedule is severely disrupted. He has Hypothyroidism. He reports no visual aura or numbness. On examination: about 9 headache days a month, BP 123/70 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 64 kg. Neurological examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Migraine. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a headache diary, sleep and eat at regular times, and limit screen time. Follow-up in 3 months with the headache diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-23 10:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Abdul Gazi, 43, male. Mr. Gazi returns for review reporting normal heart tests, a persistent fear of dying, and sudden attacks of a racing heart. His first attack happened at a busy market in Sirajganj. He works as a construction worker and experiences high daily stress. He has Essential hypertension. He denies chest pain or shortness of breath outside of attacks. On examination: about 3 panic attacks in the last month, BP 151/95 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, weight 48 kg. Mood is anxious with clear apprehension. Assessment: Panic disorder. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to practise slow breathing during attacks, reduce caffeine intake, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-07-23 11:00 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Ehsan Hossain, 25, male. Mr. Hossain presents with pain behind his eyes, severe aching in his bones and muscles, and a sudden high fever. His illness started during the monsoon after mosquitoes bred in water tanks near Bogura. He works as a nurse and denies any prior chronic medical conditions. He reports no bleeding manifestations. On examination: temperature 103.2°F, platelet count 97000 per microlitre, BP 118/70 mmHg, pulse 95 bpm, weight 73 kg. Abdomen is soft without hepatomegaly. Assessment: Dengue fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to drink at least three litres of fluid a day, avoid ibuprofen and aspirin, repeat the platelet count in 48 hours, and go to hospital at once for bleeding gums, black stools, or severe belly pain. Follow-up in 48 hours with a repeat platelet count.

Visit note | 2025-07-23 11:00 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Jui Shikder, 44, female. Mrs. Shikder returns for review complaining of waking up tired and having trouble falling asleep most nights. Her sleep problems began after starting rotating shifts at a factory in Faridpur. On examination: Insomnia Severity Index score 18, BP 117/85 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 55 kg. She appears fatigued but alert. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up in 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-07-23 11:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Sabbir Shikder, 51, male.
